newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese premier sees sustained economic boom.
newsitem.headline: Chinese premier sees sustained economic boom.

text.p: China is on course for a 15-year economic boom, with annual gross national product growth to roar along at an average eight percent until 2000 and seven percent in the decade after, Premier Li Peng said on Thursday.

Far-reaching reforms and opening to the outside world had left the economy in good shape to maintain momentum and boost China's power, Li told a conference of international parliamentarians in Beijing.
China had enjoyed average annual gross national product (GNP) growth of nine percent over 18 years of reform, Li said.

"We now envisage an average annual GNP growth rate of eight percent for the remaining five years of this century and seven percent for the first 10 years of the next century," he told a session of the 96th Inter-Parliamentary Conference.
"This will further upgrade China's aggregate national strength and (the) people's livelihood," he said.
China would never be a threat to its neighbours and resolutely opposed all hegemonism and power politics, he said, adding that fears of Beijing's growing power were misplaced.

In his speech to the five-day conference, a talking shop for more than 600 members of parliament from 120 countries, Li painted a picture of China as a haven of ethnic harmony where the protection of human rights was a sacred cause.
His description was in sharp contrast to the comments of some delegates who took part in a rare free debate on human rights on Tuesday.
Norwegian and Austrian parliamentarians then called on Beijing to ease repression in Tibet, where China has launched tough campaigns to crush pro-independence activists.
Li said China would stand strongly against anyone who interfered in its internal affairs under the pretexts of human rights or ethnic or religious issues.
"No country has the right to interfere in the internal affairs of other countries," he said.
